title: Keenan Allen returns to Colts practice after OVWI arrest
content:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was at practice Tuesday morning after being arrested early Sunday morning and charged with two misdemeanors for operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated. Allen, 34, was released from the Marion County Jail around 4 p.m. ET Sunday. He has a court date set for Sept. 16, three days after the Colts’ season opener against the Baltimore Ravens.

The Colts had to cut down their roster to 53 by Sunday night, but did not release Allen following his arrest. Given his otherwise clean off-field record and his importance to the offense, that shouldn’t be a surprise.

“Good people make mistakes,” Colts general manager Chris Ballard said Tuesday. “He’s a tremendous human being. Give him some grace, and he’ll work through the process of the legal system.

“Holy s—. We want to freaking kill people when they …  One mistake in a 14-year career, yes, but give people grace. One of the problems we have right now is we don’t give anybody grace. I think over time, and he understands this, he will prove to y’all and this city who he is. And I think he’ll do that in a short amount of time.”

Ballard said Allen will be available to play in Week 1. When asked if Allen will be punished by the team, Ballard said, “We’ll keep that internal.”

In terms of facing punishment from the league, given the NFL’s track record of taking its time before it makes a decision on such matters, Allen may not be punished (or suspended) for a while, meaning it’s possible he could play the entire season without having to miss time.

Allen was charged with DWI/DUI/OWI endangering a person and DWI/DUI/OWI with a blood alcohol level of .08 or more, according to an Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department report. The charges Allen faces are Class A and C misdemeanors, respectively. A Class A misdemeanor carries a penalty of up to one year in jail and a maximum fine of $5,000, per Indiana law. A Class C misdemeanor carries a penalty of up to 60 days in jail and a maximum fine of $500.

Allen was arrested Sunday morning after Indianapolis police conducted a traffic investigation involving Allen in the 100 block of South Meridian Street, according to the police report. Officers investigated after observing a vehicle parked in a no-parking zone, according to an IMPD statement.

“Officers spoke to the driver, later identified as 34-year-old Keenan Allen, and noticed signs of intoxication,” IMPD said in its statement.

Allen joined the Colts on a one-year deal worth up to $8.32 million earlier this month. Allen, who made his preseason debut Sunday, is one of just 18 players in NFL history with 1,000 receptions. He has recorded more catches (1,055), receiving yards (12,051) and touchdowns (70) than the rest of the Colts’ receivers combined.
